Center]] |champion= |bowl= [[2018 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |bowl_result= Quarterfinals }} {{2017–18 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2017–18 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[downtown Louisville|downtown Louisville, Kentucky]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They were led by interim head coach [[David Padgett]] after former head coach [[Rick Pitino]] was fired due to an [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal|FBI investigation]] into the school.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/with-rick-pitino-on-leave-assistant-david-padgett-to-be-louisville-interim-head-coach/|title=With Rick Pitino on leave, assistant David Padgett to be Louisville interim head coach|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-09-29|language=en}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21061969/how-louisville-coach-david-padgett-dealing-being-acting-head-coach-chaos-all-louisville|title=Locked out of Rick Pitino's office, David Padgett is trying to lock in at Louisville|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-10-18}} They finished the season 22–14 overall, and 9–9 in [[2017–18 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC conference play]], finishing in a tie for 8th with [[2017–18 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]], who they defeated in the second round of the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before losing to [[2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the quarterfinals. They received an invitation to the [[2018 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], where they defeated [[2017–18 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|Northern Kentucky]] in the first round and [[2017-18 Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders men's basketball team|Middle Tennessee]] in the second round before being defeated in the quarterfinals by [[2017–18 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]]. Following their NIT quarterfinal loss, Louisville announced that Padgett would not be retained as head coach.{{cite news|url=https://247sports.com/Article/David-Padgett-Louisville-part-ways-116528705|title=David Padgett, Louisville part ways|first=Evan|last=Daniels|website=247sports.com|date=March 21, 2018|accessdate=March 21, 2018}} On March 27, 2018, [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] head coach [[Chris Mack (basketball)|Chris Mack]] was hired by Louisville.{{cite news|last1=Greer|first1=Jeff|title=Louisville hires Chris Mack as new men's basketball coach|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/03/27/louisville-basketball-chris-mack-hired-xavier-coach/418999002/|accessdate=March 27, 2018|publisher=Courier Journal|date=March 27, 2018}} ==Previous season== The [[2016–17 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Cardinals]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] with a record of 25–9, 12–6 in [[2016–17 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for second place. They lost to [[2016–17 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2017 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400945793|title=Duke vs. Louisville - Game Recap - March 9, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-09-26}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 2 seed in the Midwest Region.{{Cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2017/03/12/louisville-basketball-ncaa-tournament-seed-schedule-region/99052020/|title=U of L gets No. 2 seed in Midwest Region|work=The Courier-Journal|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}} They defeated #15 [[2016–17 Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball team|Jacksonville State]] in the First Round{{Cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/march-madness/index.ssf/2017/03/louisville_vs_jacksonville_sta.html|title=Louisville downs Jacksonville State in the NCAA Tournament: Score, stats, live updates Louisville|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}} ==FBI investigation== {{main|2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal}} On September 26, 2017, federal prosecutors in New York announced that the school was under investigation for an alleged "pay for play" scheme involving recruits at Louisville.{{Cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/news/2017/09/26/university-louisville-college-basketball-fbi-sting/703414001/|title=University of Louisville college basketball program targeted in FBI investigation|work=The Courier-Journal|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/college-basketball-coaches-allegedly-took-bribes-agents-deliver-athletes-n804781|title=College basketball bribery scandal exposes "dark underbelly" of NCAA, prosecutor says|work=NBC News|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}} The allegations state that an [[Adidas]] executive conspired to pay $100,000 to the family of a top-ranked national recruit to play at Louisville and to represent Adidas when he turned pro.{{Cite news|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/news/2017/09/26/university-louisville-college-basketball-fbi-sting/703414001/|title=University of Louisville college basketball program targeted in FBI investigation|work=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}} The criminal complaint does not name Louisville specifically but appears to involve the recruitment of [[Brian Bowen]], a late, surprise commit to the school.{{Cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2017/09/26/university-louisville-recruits-college-basketball-scandal/703820001/|title=University of Louisville scandal: Brian Bowen's mom says she 'didn't know anything'|work=The Courier-Journal|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/9/26/16367526/louisville-fbi-investigation-college-basketball-scandal-rick-pitino|title=Louisville basketball has an FBI investigation to worry about while still on NCAA probation|work=SBNation.com|access-date=2017-09-26}} On September 27, head coach Rick Pitino and athletic director [[Tom Jurich]] were placed on administrative leave.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/20834710/louisville-head-coach-rick-pitino-athletic-director-tom-jurich-out|title=Louisville's Pitino and Jurich placed on leave|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-09-27}} Assistant coach David Padgett was named interim head coach on September 29. On October 6, the school also placed associate head coach [[Kenny Johnson (basketball)|Kenny Johnson]] and assistant coach Jordan Fair on administrative leave.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/20935925/louisville-cardinals-place-assistant-coaches-kenny-johnson-jordan-fair-paid-leave|title=Louisville suspends two assistants amid inquiry|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-10-06}} On October 11, Louisville announced that [[Trent Johnson]], former head coach at [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], was hired as an assistant coach.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/20992081/louisville-acting-head-coach-david-padgett-hires-trent-johnson-assistant-coach|title=David Padgett hires ex-head coach Trent Johnson as assistant|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-10-12}} On the same day, the school announced assistant coach Jordan Fair had been fired.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/fbi-fallout-louisville-announces-mens-basketball-assistant-jordan-fair-fired-without-cause/|title=Louisville announces men's basketball assistant Jordan Fair fired without cause|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-10-18|language=en}} On October 19, Louisville hired former [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] assistant [[Greg Paulus]] as an assistant.{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/10/19/louisville-interim-coach-padgett-adds-paulus-as-an-assistant/106810960/|title=Louisville interim
